completion:
Explain the form you will be issuing / what actions need to be taken.
3. If appropriate, explain the legislation applicable to the item (e.g., carcass shredders).
4. Explain the risk.
5. Explain what the patient needs to do.

**Note!** All aspects of the safety check (visual inspection, insulation resistance testing, protective circuits & earth continuity testing) should be documented along with any recommendations for repairs.

Where the appliance makes a satisfactory test, simply consider it as checking the boxes. Do not give opinions on items you are not qualified for; e.g., safety switches. # Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

Testing accuracy is paramount. This may include disconnected the downpipes (so the carers don't drop!

However, this documentation is a legal document and must be accurate. The final report is a summary of the inct come from the electrical competent task!
